physical_harm: Grievous injuries caused to vital parts of the body, including incised wounds near the chest and stomach
premeditation_planning: The court found that the accused did not act in the heat of the moment and there was premeditation
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimony of the injured eye-witnesses PW7 and PW8, and the nature of the grievous injuries caused by the use of a dagger on vital parts of the body.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly PW7 and PW8, as credible, noting their status as injured eye-witnesses and the high evidentiary value of their statements.
trial_duration: Dates of offence not stated; Trial judgment dated 01.07.2019; High Court decision dated 01.07.2019; Supreme Court decision dated 12 November 2021
legal_representation: Shree Prakash Sinha, Ms. Mohua Sinha, Rakesh Mishra, Nawalendra Kumar, Shekhar Kumar, Advs. for the Appellants; Arunabh Chowdhury, AAG, Ms. Barnali Chowdhury, Ms. Pragya Baghel, Shantanu Sagar, Vishnu Sharma, Abhishek Roy, Advs. for the Respondent
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction upheld; High Court: Conviction upheld; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants stabbed PW-7 and PW-8 with daggers in vital parts of their bodies, causing grievous injuries, and that the injuries were severe enough to fall under Section 307 IPC read with Section 34.
defence_argument: The defence submitted that the case may fall under Section 323 IPC, suggesting that the injuries were not grievous enough to warrant conviction under Section 307 IPC.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the intention of the accused must be ascertained from the weapon used, the part of the body assaulted, and the nature of the injury caused, particularly when the injury is on a vital part of the body.
precedent_relied_upon: State of M.P. v. Mansingh (2003) 10 SCC 414; Mahesh Balmiki v. State of M.P. (2000) 1 SCC 319; Jai Narain Mishra and Ors. v. State of Bihar (1971) 3 SCC 762
